entry.title: Post-Quantum Migration of Wi-Fi Key Establishment: A Hybrid ML-KEM Design for OWE and FILS, Validated on OWE with hostapd
entry.summary:
The key agreements that protect a Wi-Fi connection rely on Diffie-Hellman, which a sufficiently capable quantum computer would break; an adversary can therefore record an association today and decrypt its traffic years later. Key establishment is thus the part of IEEE 802.11 that has to be migrated first. This work targets the two protocols that perform that agreement inside the frames used to set up the link: Opportunistic Wireless Encryption (OWE), which encrypts otherwise open networks, and Fast Initial Link Setup (FILS), designed for fast connection in dense and mobile deployments.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #networking

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

entry.title: The Geometry of Zero Knowledge: Tight Masking and Efficient Multilinear Arguments
entry.summary:
Zero-knowledge proofs have become a fundamental tool for verifiable computation and privacy-preserving applications, driving growing interest in proof systems that are both succinct and efficient. In polynomial-based arguments, however, achieving zero knowledge introduces additional costs. Random masks must hide the evaluations and intermediate messages revealed during verification while preserving the underlying computation.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Strong Traceable Secret Sharing Schemes. Traceable secret sharing complements traditional schemes by enabling the identification of parties who sell their shares.
entry.summary:
Traceable secret sharing complements traditional schemes by enabling the identification of parties who sell their shares. More precisely, a group of corrupted parties generates a reconstruction box $R$ that, given enough valid shares as input, reconstructs the secret. The goal is to trace $R$ back to at least one of the corrupted parties using only black-box access to it.

entry.title: Improved Differential-Linear Cryptanalysis of Orthros, Gleeok, ZIP-AES, and ZIP-GIFT
entry.summary:
We improve differential-linear distinguishers and derive key-recovery attacks on reduced-round versions of the PRFs Orthros, Gleeok, ZIP-AES, ZIP-GIFT-64, and ZIP-GIFT-128. Relative to previous differential-linear analyses, we extend the reported coverage for Orthros from 7 to 9 rounds and for Gleeok-128 from 4 to 5 rounds. For Orthros and Gleeok-128, we obtain estimated correlation magnitudes $2^{-61.40}$ and $2^{-31.71}$, respectively.

entry.title: Practical Keyword SPIR with Lightweight Clients: Hintless and Efficient
entry.summary:
Keyword private information retrieval (keyword PIR) enables a client to retrieve the value associated with a keyword without revealing the queried keyword, generalizing traditional index PIR. This work advances the state of the art of Hao et al. (USENIX Security 2025) by addressing several key limitations of their constructions, most notably the efficiency bottleneck of their generic framework and the over-revealing nature of their more efficient designs.

entry.title: Unconditional Unclonable Encryption
entry.summary:
We give an unconditional construction of information-theoretically secure one-time private-key unclonable encryption for one-bit messages, with efficient encryption and decryption and exponentially small unclonable-indistinguishability advantage. Previous work by Bhattacharyya and Culf (Nature Physics, 2026) and Bhattacharyya, Broadbent, and Culf (arXiv:2603.08916) either only showed inverse-polynomial security loss or required inefficient encryption/decryption operations; we avoid both of these caveats. Our scheme's key is a uniformly random non-identity phase-free Pauli on $n$ qubits, and bit $a$ is encrypted as a random $(-1)^a$ eigenstate of that Pauli.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #quantum-computing

entry.title: One Fell Swoop: A Single-Trace Key-Recovery Attack on the Falcon Signing Algorithm
entry.summary:
Falcon, a lattice-based signature scheme selected for NIST post-quantum standardization, is notable for its compact signature size alongside a complex signing procedure involving extensive floating-point arithmetic. Prior side-channel attacks on Falcon signing, while demonstrating vulnerabilities, have consistently required a large number of power traces for successful key recovery, which limits their real-world practicality. This paper presents a new single-trace attack on the Falcon signing procedure.

entry.title: Zero-Knowledge IOPPs for Constrained Interleaved Codes
entry.summary:
Succinct arguments based on interactive oracle proofs (IOPs) have achieved remarkable efficiency improvements and are now widely adopted in applications. State-of-the-art IOPs involve protocols for testing proximity to constrained interleaved linear codes, and enjoy essentially optimal parameters. However, recent IOP constructions provide no privacy guarantees, which remain a must for many applications.
